title: A wait for workers ends when a watched worker process has ended, so a background wait costs the orchestrator no turn until something moved
goal: coord.py wait takes --pid PID (repeatable) and returns with exit 0, naming the pid, as soon as a watched process has ended; a watched process that is alive and no event keep the wait going until --timeout

run:
import os,subprocess as s,sys,tempfile,time
d=tempfile.mkdtemp();st=os.path.join(d,"c.sqlite")
def w(pid,t):return s.run([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--store",st,"wait","--since","0","--timeout",str(t),"--pid",str(pid)],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=60)
gone=int(s.run(["sh","-c","sleep 3 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $!"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)
t=time.time();a=w(gone,40);dt=time.time()-t;b=w(os.getpid(),2)
print(a.returncode,round(dt,1),a.stdout[-200:],a.stderr[-150:],b.returncode,b.stdout[-120:])
sys.exit(0 if a.returncode==0 and dt<30 and str(gone) in a.stdout and b.returncode==0 and "true" in b.stdout.lower() else 1)

notes: From the 2026-10-24 telemetry and query-log analysis: coord.py wait ran 741 times in 19 runner and orchestrator sessions; 724 turns had it as their only call (5.4% of turns, 208M cache-read tokens) and about 550 of the 727 single-call waits returned under 200 characters, the reply {events: [], timed_out: true}. Only 18 of the 746 waits ran in the background: the sprint skill sets --timeout 540 with a Bash timeout of 600000, so the session wakes every nine minutes, where a background command lives up to 7200000 ms and re-invokes the session when it exits. Hand-written pid waits beside it: 838 'while kill -0 PID' or 'until grep -q' loops, 342 turns that were nothing else (49M cache-read tokens), 810 sleep calls, because dispatch --detach prints a pid and tells the reader to wait for it (bl_dispatch.py:988). Saves about 900 turns, about 45 USD a week (estimate). coord wait --item already returns on a matching event and --timeout takes any length; what is missing is the dead worker (no event) and the skill's text. Also wanted, not read by the planted check: the sprint skill's waiting paragraph runs the wait as a background command (run_in_background) and names no pid loop, and dispatch --detach's message no longer says to wait for the pid. The consumer side of EP-nij36lt7, whose goal names one wait instead of polling pids. Lane: parked sprint-orchestration class, EP-gzr4mmkm.
